item.title: Jawn <= 1.4.2 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The Jawn WordPress theme, in all versions up to and including 1.4.2, contains an unauthenticated privilege escalation flaw that lets a remote attacker elevate themselves to administrator. The advisory classifies it as incorrect privilege assignment. No patched version is available.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-e0642c85-ee01-497c-8dc3-42e3ffc02995.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Firebase Authentication < 1.7.1 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Account Takeover
item.description:
The Firebase Authentication plugin for WordPress did not properly verify the email supplied in a session request. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this to log in as any existing user, including administrators, resulting in full account takeover. Version 1.7.1 fixes the issue.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f39d1f86-17d7-4b22-ba42-e88e96111bd6.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Automation Web Platform <= 4.8.6 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via 'otp_transient' Token Disclosure
item.description:
The Automation Web Platform plugin (Notifications and OTP for WooCommerce, Advanced Country Code) through 4.8.6 leaks its secret magic login token in the response to a publicly accessible OTP request. `handle_email_otp_return()` returns the token to the caller instead of delivering it only to the user's email address. An unauthenticated attacker who knows a user's email address can log in as that user, including an administrator. Version 4.8.7 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-7e473896-d94c-4f6a-a96c-bb90902532cc.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Mailgun for WordPress <= 2.2.0 - Unauthenticated Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via 'addresses' Array Keys
item.description:
The Mailgun for WordPress plugin (<= 2.2.0) lets unauthenticated users drive requests to arbitrary Mailgun API endpoints. `add_list()` takes array keys from `$_POST['addresses']` and passes them through `sanitize_text_field()`, which does not stop path traversal, so the keys end up in the Mailgun API request path. The request is authenticated with the site's Mailgun API key. Version 2.2.1 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-110e888d-69fc-4682-b908-2b62288c5227.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: JSON Options <= 0.0.4 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:
The JSON Options plugin, in all versions up to and including 0.0.4, allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server. The advisory attributes this to insufficient validation of user-supplied input before it is executed (code injection). No patched version exists.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5c601f75-3ee2-47ed-8d67-67fac4403a5d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WS Form LITE <= 1.10.80 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection via Form Submission
item.description:
WS Form LITE up to and including 1.10.80 deserializes untrusted input taken from form submission meta values, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP objects (CWE-502). The plugin itself contains no known POP chain, so exploitability depends on another installed plugin or theme providing one. Version 1.10.82 fixes the issue.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-df36eae9-6f2b-432c-a765-57450939b344.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Broken Link Checker < 2.4.12 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:
The Broken Link Checker plugin contains an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability caused by insufficient validation of user-supplied input before it is executed (CWE-94, code injection). An unauthenticated attacker can run arbitrary code on the server. The issue is fixed in 2.4.12.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-fd3b95ce-3051-4b41-8bf4-362fa6be6ce5.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: The WP Remote WordPress Plugin, Malcare Security, and BlogVault Backup & Staging < 6.65 - Unauthenticated Site Takeover via Brute Force
item.description:
The WP Remote, MalCare Security, and BlogVault Backup & Staging plugins, all versions before 6.65, generate the values used by their remote-connection feature with a weak pseudo-random number generator (CWE-338). An unauthenticated attacker can brute force those values and connect the site to their own remote management service, which gives them control of the site. Version 6.65 is the patched release for all three plugins.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-01f287b6-1720-4ece-9141-f906835b8bae.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ShopBuilder Pro – Elementor WooCommerce Builder Addons <= 2.2.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion
item.description:
ShopBuilder Pro (Elementor WooCommerce Builder Addons) through 2.2.0 fails to properly validate file paths in a code path reachable without authentication. An unauthenticated attacker can delete arbitrary files on the server. Deleting a file such as `wp-config.php` can lead to remote code execution, which is why the issue is rated critical. No patched version is available.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-2c1b53b9-e70b-4204-a00e-8745611606bf.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload for Contact Form 7 < 1.3.9.9 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:
Drag and Drop Multiple File Upload for Contact Form 7 has an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CWE-94, code injection) caused by insufficient validation of user-supplied input before it is executed. Any remote attacker can run arbitrary code on the server without logging in. The issue is fixed in 1.3.9.9.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-30cc4552-bd12-4211-bd06-637352ceb5df.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WooCommerce File Approval <= 10.7 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion
item.description:
The WooCommerce File Approval plugin does not sufficiently validate file paths in all versions up to and including 10.7. Unauthenticated attackers can use this path traversal flaw to delete arbitrary files on the server. Deleting a file such as `wp-config.php` can lead to remote code execution, for example by forcing the site back into the installer flow. No patched version is available.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-35876ad9-595b-4099-b309-21bb80304baa.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SMS Alert – SMS & OTP for WooCommerce, Order Notifications & Abandoned Cart Recovery < 3.9.8 - Authentication Bypass via Account Takeover
item.description:
The SMS Alert plugin (SMS & OTP for WooCommerce, order notifications, abandoned cart recovery) has a critical authentication bypass in versions before 3.9.8. Unauthenticated attackers can take over other users' accounts, including administrators. The fix shipped in 3.9.8.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-6b8ba516-54f8-4422-846a-106b9e8bca8d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Kirki – Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer < 6.2.1 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:
The Kirki plugin (Freeform Page Builder, Website Builder & Customizer) has a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability. User-supplied input is executed on the server without sufficient validation. Version 6.2.1 contains the fix.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ee755e25-5f70-4688-b08d-4a3f127d91d4.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: MasterStudy LMS WordPress Plugin – for Online Courses and Education <= 3.7.42 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion
item.description:
MasterStudy LMS versions up to and including 3.7.42 fail to properly validate file paths in a code path reachable without authentication, allowing an attacker to delete arbitrary files on the server. Deleting a file such as `wp-config.php` can force WordPress back into the installer flow and lead to remote code execution. The issue is fixed in 3.7.43.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-fa8f0688-8c54-43f8-acea-2aec2fcfbdce.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ManageWP Worker < 4.9.37 - Authentication Bypass
item.description:
The ManageWP Worker plugin, which lets the ManageWP dashboard remotely administer a site, has an authentication bypass in all versions before 4.9.37. An unauthenticated attacker can log in as another user, including an administrator. The fix ships in 4.9.37.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-2cd71719-e900-46c8-884e-b485c62fed00.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ACPT (Premium) <= 2.0.63 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The premium ACPT plugin, in all versions up to and including 2.0.63, lets unauthenticated attackers elevate their privileges because it does not sufficiently restrict the capabilities a user can grant themselves. The flaw is rated critical (CVSS 9.8). Wordfence lists no known patch.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-44c0c0a0-94a4-4394-b661-1ce53d63f789.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: TranslatePress – Multilingual <= 3.3.1 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Password Reset Link Disclosure
item.description:
TranslatePress – Multilingual <= 3.3.1 exposes administrator password-reset URLs to unauthenticated users through the `trp_get_translations_regular` AJAX action. When a reset email is generated for an admin whose profile locale is a published secondary language, the URL (including the plaintext reset key and login parameters) is saved as a translatable string in the dictionary table, and the AJAX action can return it. An attacker can use it to take over the administrator account. Version 3.3.2 fixes the issue.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4f4ebf09-b089-4118-a0ee-399243253f9c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Avada <= 7.16 and Fusion Builder <= 3.16 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Arbitrary File Write
item.description:
Avada theme versions up to 7.16, when paired with an active Fusion Builder plugin at 3.16 or below, allow unauthenticated attackers to write attacker-controlled files to the server. Because the written files can be PHP, this escalates to remote code execution and full site compromise. The flaw is a chain of missing authorization and input validation weaknesses spanning both components. Fixed in Avada 7.16.1 and Fusion Builder 3.16.1.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5bef5bd3-8ec9-4a5b-bcdd-98952c7ef390.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ERP: Complete HR, Accounting & CRM Suite Built for WooCommerce <= 1.17.8 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via CRM Email Connect IMAP Attachment
item.description:
The ERP: Complete HR, Accounting & CRM Suite Built for WooCommerce plugin (<= 1.17.8) writes inbound IMAP email attachments to disk in `save_attachments()` without validating the file extension or normalizing the filename. An unauthenticated attacker can email the site's configured inbound mailbox with an attachment named like `../helper.php`, and the cron-driven IMAP sync will write that PHP file outside the protected `crm-attachments` directory and into `wp-content/uploads/`. Version 1.17.9 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-b9d11eb9-5e18-459f-a9d4-cccb1d593402.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Tutor LMS <= 4.0.5 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Zero-Argument Function Invocation
item.description:
Tutor LMS through 4.0.5 has an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw. A template-rendering path calls `extract()` on a request-influenced `$data` array, which lets an attacker overwrite the internal `$method_map` lookup table. A dynamic `is_callable()` dispatch then invokes whatever zero-argument PHP function the attacker names and returns its output. Version 4.0.6 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-37848512-fbdf-48cd-9d59-5bfb1bdbe73d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SmilePass Selfie Login <= 1.0.2 - Authentication Bypass to Administrator
item.description:
The SmilePass Selfie Login plugin, in all versions up to and including 1.0.2, contains an authentication bypass that lets unauthenticated attackers log in as arbitrary existing users, including administrators. No patched version is available. The source record does not describe the vulnerable code path.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-a98b31a5-2aac-439f-a081-445dba4522e2.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WPMU DEV Dashboard <= 5.0.1 - Authentication Bypass to Administrator via SSO HMAC Canonicalization Confusion
item.description:
The WPMU DEV Dashboard plugin's Hub SSO flow builds its HMAC over inconsistent messages in its two unauthenticated AJAX steps. `wdpsso_step1` signs and discloses an unseparated concatenation of token, state, redirect, and domain. `wdpsso_step2` verifies an unseparated concatenation that omits domain. An unauthenticated attacker can take a valid HMAC from step 1 and replay it to step 2, which yields an authenticated administrator session. Version 5.0.2 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3d4321c8-15a4-46f5-9b0e-2098a7fcfb5b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Sigma Forms Pro <= 1.4.5 - Unauthenticated Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload Leading to Remote Code Execution via Pre-built Template File Upload Field
item.description:
Sigma Forms Pro (SigmaForms Pro – AI Generated Forms) up to 1.4.5 lets unauthenticated attackers upload arbitrary files, including PHP, through form submissions. `handle_form_submission` dynamically grants the `unfiltered_upload` capability to all users during submission and skips MIME type validation when a file field has no `allowed_file_types` configured. Several default pre-built templates ship with unrestricted file upload fields, so the flaw is exploitable on a fresh install. Version 1.4.6 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-44d63454-87f0-49e3-ac04-2fa83882500d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: GiveWP – Donation Plugin and Fundraising Platform <= 4.16.7.1 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection to Remote Code Execution
item.description:
GiveWP through 4.16.7.1 has an unauthenticated PHP Object Injection that chains to remote code execution. An attacker can register a donor account through GiveWP's registration handler and store a serialized object in the `last_name` profile field. The legacy donation flow then preserves that object in the GiveWP session, and a later request unserializes the session without restricting allowed classes. A usable POP chain through TCPDF and GiveWP's `ProviderForwarder` trait allows arbitrary OS command execution. The fix is in 4.16.7.2.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-49c3be3f-60b3-4b83-9683-a08e8e1cf9e9.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Hash Form – Drag & Drop Form Builder <= 1.4.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload
item.description:
The Hash Form – Drag & Drop Form Builder plugin fails to validate file types on upload in versions up to and including 1.4.2. Unauthenticated attackers can upload arbitrary files to the server, which may lead to remote code execution. The issue is fixed in 1.4.3.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-60dacb8d-0de6-4755-8857-6b05083a23b8.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Shared Files Pro < 1.7.68 & Shared Files Free < 1.7.67 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion
item.description:
The Shared Files plugin (Free and Pro) failed to sufficiently validate file paths before deleting files, allowing unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server. Deleting a critical file such as `wp-config.php` can lead to remote code execution, for example by forcing the site back into the installer. The fix is in Shared Files 1.7.67 (Free) and Shared Files Pro 1.7.68.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-bdb4468a-cd01-4f4c-9353-d77fcf7a558f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Newspapers X 1.0.46 - 1.0.48 - Backdoor
item.description:
Versions 1.0.46 through 1.0.48 of the Newspapers X theme shipped with embedded malicious code, a backdoor that lets unauthenticated attackers achieve remote code execution on the site. The issue is fixed in 1.0.49. Any site running an affected version should be treated as potentially compromised, not merely vulnerable.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-eb075839-5669-4a5a-b225-f7ea98672490.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Custom User Registration Fields for WooCommerce <= 2.2.3 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'afreg_select_user_role' Parameter in Store API Checkout
item.description:
Custom User Registration Fields for WooCommerce <= 2.2.3 lets unauthenticated visitors pick their own user role during WooCommerce Store API checkout. The plugin stores the submitted `afreg_select_user_role` value in order meta and later passes it to `WP_User::add_role()` without checking it against the admin-configured list of allowed roles. An attacker can submit `administrator` and become an admin. Version 2.2.4 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-715723e7-5820-4a64-848f-f89b5b73a681.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: MyHome Core <= 4.4.5 - Authentication Bypass to Account Takeover via Activation Token
item.description:
MyHome Core versions up to and including 4.4.5 allow unauthenticated attackers to take over unconfirmed user accounts, including administrators. The `send_link()` AJAX handler lacks an authorization check and lets anyone generate an activation token for an arbitrary unconfirmed account. The `activate()` function then validates that token improperly and issues a valid authentication cookie. Version 4.4.6 patches it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c458e018-5901-4917-9847-35f07646e068.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WPLP Cookie Consent – Cookie Banner & Consent Management for GDPR, CCPA & Google Consent Mode <= 4.4.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload
item.description:
The WPLP Cookie Consent plugin (<= 4.4.1) lacks file type validation on an upload handler that unauthenticated users can reach. An attacker can place arbitrary files on the server, which may lead to remote code execution. Version 4.4.2 fixes the issue.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4a47660e-67a6-42d4-a7ec-911dcf3e6e47.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Advanced Custom Fields: Extended < 0.9.2.7 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Administrator Account Takeover
item.description:
Advanced Custom Fields: Extended contained an unauthenticated account-takeover flaw: the plugin changed a user's password without first verifying the requester's identity. Any remote attacker could set a new password for an arbitrary account, including an administrator, and then log in as that user. Version 0.9.2.7 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-72a179af-25a0-40f2-a585-8d25c0289782.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WPLP Cookie Consent <= 4.4.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via 'upload-logo' REST Endpoint
item.description:
WPLP Cookie Consent through 4.4.1 lets unauthenticated attackers upload arbitrary files to the server. `saas_upload_logo()` performs no file type validation, and the plugin's WPLP connector REST endpoints (including `upload-logo`) have an authorization bypass that exposes it to anonymous requests. Uploading an executable file such as PHP may lead to remote code execution. Version 4.4.2 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-96a2a552-e73f-4b27-88de-50eb63a8d131.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Nokri - Job Board WordPress Theme <= 1.6.6 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'token' Parameter
item.description:
The Nokri job board theme's `nokri_reset_password()` function validates the password reset token insufficiently. An attacker can submit an empty `token` value, and it matches users whose `sb_password_forget_token` user meta is empty or unset. That lets an unauthenticated attacker reset the password of any such account, including administrators, and take it over. Version 1.6.7 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-b03b7ea8-6485-495d-b815-2b7b882a75a2.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Booking for Appointments and Events Calendar – Amelia (Premium) 8.0 - 9.6.2 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Administrator via 'externalId'
item.description:
Amelia (Premium) 8.0 through 9.6.2 has an unauthenticated privilege escalation. The customer update endpoint does not validate the attacker-controlled `type` parameter, so a caller can set their role to `manager`. When `externalId` is `0`, this triggers creation of a WordPress user with the `wpamelia-manager` role. The manager role can then be used to create a provider entity linked to an administrator user ID and overwrite that administrator's password. The issue is fixed in 9.6.3.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-0c2266b8-cc23-46de-bc80-09e3d6294854.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Authorizer <= 3.15.1 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation
item.description:
The Authorizer plugin (<= 3.15.1) contains an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability. Per the advisory, the plugin insufficiently restricts the capabilities a user can grant themselves, so an unauthenticated attacker can elevate their privileges beyond those intended for their role. The issue is fixed in 3.15.2.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3f211911-b8e1-4ee2-ad4a-189c58fdbe8d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: SigmaForms Pro <= 1.4.11 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Deletion via Path Traversal in File Upload Field
item.description:
SigmaForms Pro – AI Generated Forms <= 1.4.11 does not validate file paths in `delete_submission_files`. An unauthenticated attacker can submit a path traversal value through a form's file upload field. The value is stored with the submission, and when an administrator deletes that submission in the admin panel, the plugin deletes the file the path points to. Version 1.4.12 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c714e2b3-8a96-4078-99a4-4ce620939828.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: JetFormBuilder — Dynamic Blocks Form Builder < 3.6.5.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Shortcode Execution
item.description:
JetFormBuilder (Dynamic Blocks Form Builder) contained an unauthenticated arbitrary shortcode execution flaw. Request-supplied message content was passed through shortcode expansion before escaping was applied. In addition, `sanitize_wysiwyg()` called `wp_kses_post()` before `wp_specialchars_decode()`, so entity-encoded payloads survived sanitization and were decoded just in time for shortcode parsing. An unauthenticated attacker can inject shortcode syntax into form message content that is displayed on any page rendering a JetFormBuilder form. The issue is fixed in 3.6.5.2.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-11f367a0-3a1a-474b-8dae-b3b0f942574a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: RegistrationMagic <= 6.0.9.8 - Authentication Bypass
item.description:
RegistrationMagic (custom registration forms, user registration, payments, and login plugin) versions up to and including 6.0.9.8 contain an authentication bypass that lets unauthenticated attackers get past authentication. The flaw is rated critical (CVSS 9.8) and is fixed in 6.0.9.9. The advisory does not describe the vulnerable code path or what access the bypass grants.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-b9f75a13-76be-45b5-8ec3-a89cbb6e0256.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Divi Ajax Filter <= 5.1.2 - Unauthenticated Local File Inclusion via 'custom_loop_template' Parameter
item.description:
Divi Ajax Filter versions up to and including 5.1.2 contain an unauthenticated Local File Inclusion flaw via the `custom_loop_template` parameter. An attacker can cause the plugin to include and execute arbitrary `.php` files on the server. It is only exploitable when the `loop_templates` parameter is set to `custom-template`. The issue is fixed in 5.1.3.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-8fbb92ac-a8e7-480d-8910-416fbe902a2a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: ACPT (Premium) <= 2.0.66 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'acpt_form_post_id' Parameter
item.description:
ACPT (Premium) through 2.0.66 lets unauthenticated visitors take over any WordPress account, including administrators. The `submit()` function accepts a client-supplied target user ID (via the `acpt_form_post_id` parameter) and passes it to `wp_update_user()` without an authorization check. An attacker can overwrite the victim's email address and password. Version 2.0.67 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-abc138f5-0bb7-4ce3-a504-89580021bedb.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Mail Mint <= 1.31.0 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection in Arbitrary Form Fields
item.description:
The Mail Mint plugin passes untrusted form-submission input to PHP deserialization in its `handle_form_submission` function, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary PHP objects. Because a POP chain is present, this escalates to remote code execution on the server. Version 1.31.1 contains the fix. An earlier, incomplete patch shipped in 1.23.1.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-76c073d9-9572-43e4-82eb-49adf678535b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Hummingbird – Speed Optimization, Caching, Minify, Compress & CDN <= 3.21.0 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Cookie Name in Page Cache Debug Log
item.description:
Hummingbird's page-cache debug log can be turned into a web-accessible PHP webshell by an anonymous visitor. The log file `wp-content/wphb-logs/page-caching-log.php` is meant to be protected by a leading `<?php die(); ?>` header, but a broken `class_exists( 'Filesystem' )` guard omits that header when the file is created during a front-end request. `get_cookies()` then writes raw `wphb_cache_*` cookie names into the file unsanitized, so a single request with a crafted cookie name plants PHP that runs when the file is requested directly. Fixed in 3.21.1.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-65c3ca36-79e6-47f8-9524-27e7631f4caf.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: MStore API <= 4.20.0 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via 'id_token' Parameter JWT Forgery
item.description:
The MStore API plugin's Firebase Phone Auth login path did not verify the JWT signature on the `id_token` it received. `FirebasePhoneAuthHelper::verify_id_token()` checked the claims (`alg`, `kid`, `aud`, `iss`) but never validated the signature against Google's public certificates. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore forge a token signed with their own RSA key pair, impersonate any phone number, and log in as an existing user or create a new account. Version 4.21.1 is the patched release.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-4a1127af-74f6-4748-9aee-5a8c6c2766a4.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Post Grid and Gutenberg Blocks – ComboBlocks 2.2.85 - 2.3.22 - Unauthenticated Hook Injection
item.description:
The Post Grid and Gutenberg Blocks (ComboBlocks) plugin exposes several functions in `includes/blocks/form-wrap/function.php` that let unauthenticated visitors trigger arbitrary WordPress action hooks. The flaw affects versions 2.2.85 through 2.3.22 and is fixed in 2.3.23. The advisory rates it Critical.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-ec8666d4-042e-4cf4-86f5-474a69d90ff6.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: MemberDash <= 1.8.5 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via Insecure Direct Object Reference via 'id' Parameter
item.description:
MemberDash versions up to and including 1.8.5 contain an Insecure Direct Object Reference in the registration flow. The plugin trusts a user-supplied `id` parameter without validating it, so an unauthenticated attacker can supply an arbitrary user ID during registration and change that user's password, including an administrator's. The victim receives no notification. The issue is fixed in 1.8.6.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-222e0f27-f269-4751-9544-1a6cb03ab3a7.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Frontend Admin by DynamiApps <= 3.29.12 - Unauthenticated Account Takeover via '_acf_objects' Object Identifier
item.description:
Frontend Admin by DynamiApps contains an unauthenticated authentication-bypass flaw that leads to full account takeover. The `pre_update_value` function performs no capability or ownership check, and `ActionPost::conditions_logic()` skips its `current_user_can('edit_post')` gate whenever the submitted post ID is non-numeric (for example `user_1`). An anonymous form submission can therefore be routed at an arbitrary user record and overwrite that user's email address, after which the native WordPress password-reset flow hands over the account, including administrators. The issue is fixed in 3.29.13.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f1637a3b-7b0f-485d-9d19-4f711f8c671b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Teddy Bear Customize Addon <= 1.0.5 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Account Takeover

item.title: Multi Uploader for Gravity Forms <= 1.1.9 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Chunked File Upload
item.description:

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via wpautop() Blockquote Handling
item.description:
WordPress core's `wpautop()` contains a stored XSS flaw that unauthenticated users can exploit through comment content. The paragraph-unwrapping regex `

]*)>` does not handle a `

` whose attribute region contains a `>`. When this combines with `wpautop()`'s blank-line paragraph splitting, a newline inside a blockquote `cite` value causes a `

` tag to be moved into the tag itself. The resulting malformed markup lets attacker-supplied script run when the comment is rendered. Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-1984abee-a74c-48d7-874f-c4421243e5e5.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Missing Authorization to customize_changeset Write via XML-RPC (Multisite/Custom Role edit_css Bypass)
item.description:
WordPress core's XML-RPC `_insert_post()` handler allowed internal-only builtin post types — notably `customize_changeset` — to be written through the generic post API. Doing so skipped the Customizer's per-setting capability checks, so a user who can create changesets but lacks `edit_css` (which maps to `unfiltered_css`) could write changeset values, including Additional CSS. The fix is included in the listed security releases across the 6.6 through 7.1 branches.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-28747e2e-9012-470c-a891-0fe97fd1ddba.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Authenticated (Administrator+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Custom Header Image Data
item.description:
WordPress core had a stored XSS vulnerability in the custom header feature. The `header_image_data` theme mod's width, height, and URL values were not sanitized strictly enough. `get_custom_header()` returned `width`/`height` without casting them to integers, and `Custom_Image_Header::step_1()` echoed a `style` attribute string without escaping it. A user with `edit_theme_options` could therefore store script payloads that execute on the custom-header admin screen. The patched releases fix both problems.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3d59700b-3540-464c-bd27-23bb71f9b082.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Path Traversal via REST Templates Controller
item.description:
WordPress core has a path traversal bug in `_get_block_template_file()`, the function the REST templates controller uses to resolve a template slug into a file path. The slug is turned into a path without checking that it stays inside the theme's template directory. The route regex blocks `.`, but the sanitize callback URL-decodes the value twice, so a double-encoded `../` sequence passes the regex and reaches file resolution. As a result, any authenticated user with Contributor-level access or higher can read arbitrary `.html` files outside the theme template directory through `/wp/v2/templates/<id>?source=theme`.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-64453a11-e0dd-40f8-99c3-f05ef640b42b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Ultimate Addons for Contact Form 7 3.2.4 - 3.5.50 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload
item.description:
The Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 plugin (titled "Ultimate Addons for Contact Form 7" in the advisory) lacks file type validation in a file upload path, so unauthenticated visitors can upload arbitrary files to the server. Uploading an executable file such as a PHP script may lead to remote code execution. The issue is fixed in 3.5.51.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-77b19085-4a7f-4554-bbad-46aa9ab10fc5.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Information Exposure via Sample Permalink AJAX Actions
item.description:
WordPress core's `wp_ajax_sample_permalink()` and `wp_ajax_get_permalink()` AJAX handlers did not check `edit_post` against the post ID supplied in the request. An authenticated user with Contributor-level access or higher could therefore call these actions with another user's post ID and retrieve its slug and sample permalink. This works even when the target post is a draft or pending post they cannot otherwise edit. The fix ships in security releases across six maintained branches.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-83597e50-1992-4171-b24e-b14f55be6e4c.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Authenticated (Author+) Missing Authorization to Comment/Note Reparenting via REST API
item.description:
WordPress core's REST comments controller did not check authorization against the **target** post when a comment's or note's parent post was changed. `update_item_permissions_check()` checked only the post the comment was currently attached to. A user who can edit a comment, such as an Author editing a comment on their own post, could move that comment or note onto any other post, including posts they can neither read nor edit. The patched releases fix this missing authorization check (CWE-862).
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-8b8d4431-ac72-45a2-b4a1-19690946d0ee.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Insecure Direct Object Reference to Arbitrary Post Overwrite
item.description:
WordPress core has an Insecure Direct Object Reference in `_wp_translate_postdata()`. On the post *create* path, where no `post_ID` is supplied, the function honors a raw `ID` parameter from the request. `wp_insert_post()` then treats that request as an update to the existing post with that ID. The per-post `edit_post` capability checks run only on the update path, so they are skipped. As a result, any authenticated user with Contributor-level access or above can overwrite the content of arbitrary existing posts, including posts written by Editors and Administrators.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-adc90b32-f973-4c8e-b419-0614d4642b7f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Authenticated (Author+) Information Exposure via attachment_submitbox_metadata()
item.description:
WordPress core's `attachment_submitbox_metadata()` did not check `read_post` against an attachment's parent post before exposing information about it. As a result, an authenticated user with `upload_files` (Author role and above by default) could view the **title** of a private or otherwise unreadable post that the attachment is attached to. The fix adds the missing capability check on the parent post. Patched releases are available on every affected branch.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-b54af5b0-d79a-4fb2-965f-d3ff4956dc5a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Forced Theme Install/Preview and Selector Injection via Theme Installer Route
item.description:
WordPress core's theme installer JavaScript (`theme.js`, the `RunInstaller` path) read the `theme` slug from `theme-install.php?theme=<slug>` and inserted it into a jQuery attribute selector without escaping: `$('div[data-slug="'+slug+'"]')`. The selector also matched any matching `div`, not just theme cards. As a result, a crafted URL could make the installer automatically install and preview an inactive WordPress.org theme. It could also inject an arbitrary jQuery selector into the admin page. The fix ships in the listed patched point releases.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c34ef5e3-afcd-4686-861f-5e382812233a.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - HTML API set_modifiable_text() Comment Boundary Break
item.description:
`WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::set_modifiable_text()` could produce HTML where text written into a comment node ended the comment early. The guard that checks for comment closers used the pattern `/--!?>/`, which catches `-->` and `--!>` but misses the abrupt-closing `-?>` form. Any text after that point would then be parsed as live markup. The fix hardens the guard in core's HTML API. The advisory describes it as developer-facing hardening: WordPress core has no code path of its own that makes this exploitable.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c41aadb1-e1a6-4bda-ac94-c461c320e78f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1 - Authenticated (Administrator+) Missing Authorization to Network Plugin Activation (Multisite)
item.description:
WordPress core's `wp_ajax_activate_plugin()` AJAX handler did not check the `manage_network_plugins` capability when activating a network-only plugin. On Multisite, a **site administrator** could therefore network-activate an installed plugin marked `Network: true`, which normally requires a Super Admin. Two causes combined to allow this: the missing capability check, and a path-normalization mismatch between `is_network_only_plugin()` and `activate_plugin()`. Security releases across the supported branches add the check.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-dc1ae2c7-1eff-4976-8f88-f0b97a5cf323.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Forminator Forms <= 1.57.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Shortcode Execution via 'current_url' Parameter
item.description:
Forminator Forms versions up to and including 1.57.2 pass a user-controlled value, reported as the `current_url` parameter, to `do_shortcode()` without adequate validation. An unauthenticated attacker can cause arbitrary registered shortcodes to be executed on the site. The issue is fixed in 1.57.3.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-7c28869c-c880-4322-9f17-09495a08576e.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Gravity Forms <= 3.1.0.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Hidden File Upload Field
item.description:
Gravity Forms up to and including 3.1.0.4 allows unauthenticated arbitrary file upload. A File Upload field with Visibility set to 'Hidden' skips extension validation, and a file that was rejected still carries its intact upload state into `upload_file()`, which persists it without re-validation. Files that may be executable can land on the server, making remote code execution possible. Version 3.1.1 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-787e22a9-329b-4e71-bc2a-4f5524fc9356.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WP Recipe Maker <= 10.8.1 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Shortcode Execution via Recipe Comment Content
item.description:
WP Recipe Maker <= 10.8.1 runs `do_shortcode()` recursively over every scalar in the recipe's structured metadata array in `WPRM_Metadata::sanitize_metadata()`. That array includes `reviewBody`, which is filled verbatim from the `comment_content` of approved `wprm-comment-rating` comments. A commenter can therefore put shortcode tokens in a rated comment and have them executed server-side on every render of the recipe page. The output lands in the page's JSON-LD `reviewBody` and is visible to all visitors. Version 10.8.2 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-d6ad49ff-85eb-4d05-ba23-51d89695add3.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WooCommerce Online Product Designer <= 2.14.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload
item.description:
The Web to Print Online Designer plugin (listed by Wordfence as "WooCommerce Online Product Designer") through 2.14.0 lacks file type validation on an upload handler reachable without authentication. An unauthenticated attacker can upload arbitrary files to the server, which can lead to remote code execution if a executable file such as PHP lands in a web-accessible location. Version 2.15.0 fixes the issue.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-5016ecf2-6016-4a46-8e16-30e9f79344e4.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: YAHMAN Add-ons <= 0.9.30 - Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
item.description:
The YAHMAN Add-ons plugin for WordPress has a critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in all versions up to and including 0.9.30. User-supplied input is executed on the server without sufficient validation, so an attacker needs no account to run arbitrary code. The issue is fixed in 0.9.31.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-817189e9-a4d2-4bb1-b866-fc7ae2d2be4f.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Give Tributes <= 2.3.1 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection via 'give_tributes_ecard_notify[recipient][personalized][]' Parameter
item.description:
The Give Tributes plugin (an add-on for GiveWP) deserializes untrusted input from the `give_tributes_ecard_notify[recipient][personalized][]` request parameter in versions up to and including 2.3.1, allowing unauthenticated PHP Object Injection. Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-0cdd5562-8755-4ca3-9c16-a5b364f8408b.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Meta Box AIO <= 3.7.2 And Standalone Plugin Extensions - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to Administrator to 'rwmb_frontend_field_object_id' Parameter
item.description:
Meta Box AIO and its standalone extensions contain a chained flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker become an Administrator. `populate_via_query_string()` in the mb-frontend-submission component accepts the `rwmb_frontend_field_object_id` GET parameter and overrides the form's target `object_id` with no authorization check. Because `Form::process()` lacks the `user_can_edit()` check that `render()` has, the attacker can overwrite the `post_content` of any page with an arbitrary shortcode. The injected `[mb_user_profile_register]` shortcode is then trusted by mb-user-profile, which honors its `role` and `auto_login` attributes without validation. Fixes shipped in 3.12.0 (AIO / User Profile) and 4.6.0 (Frontend Submission).
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-0951bc88-aa4e-4584-8203-9e02af322494.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: WordPress Core <= 7.1.1 - Unauthenticated Local File Inclusion via locate_template() Path Traversal
item.description:
`locate_template()` in WordPress core resolved a caller-supplied template name against the theme directories without checking that the resolved path stayed inside them. A template name containing `..` could therefore resolve to a readable `.php` file elsewhere on the server, and that file would then be included. The route an unauthenticated visitor can reach in core is `get_page_template()`, which builds `page-{$pagename}.php` from the URL-derived, url-decoded `pagename` query var. When the server also has a suitable PHP file such as `pearcmd.php` with `register_argc_argv=On`, this local file inclusion becomes remote code execution. The fix ships in point releases on every supported branch back to 4.7.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-6ff76d9b-aa12-4391-90cd-f9df36d4a3a5.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Paytium: Mollie payment forms & donations <= 5.0.3 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'pt_form_field[pt-user-role]' Parameter
item.description:
Paytium <= 5.0.3 allows unauthenticated attackers to create an administrator account. The 5.0.3 fix added a `wp_hash()`/`hash_equals()` signature check on the `pt-paytium-user-data` field, but a second filter, `pt_cf_checkout_meta()` on the `pt_meta_values` hook, still copies every `$_POST['pt_form_field'][*]` key into the payment meta without verification. A forged `pt-user-role` value therefore overwrites the signed builder's output and is later passed to `wp_insert_user()` as the role. Version 5.0.4 is the patched release.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-caa1a42a-6bb2-42c8-aae7-fb1c895573a8.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Visual Composer Website Builder <= 45.16.0 - Unauthenticated Local File Inclusion via 'vcv-template' Parameter
item.description:
The Visual Composer Website Builder plugin contains an unauthenticated Local File Inclusion vulnerability in versions up to and including 45.16.0. The `vcv-template` parameter is used to select a file that the server includes and executes, and it is not adequately restricted. An unauthenticated attacker can make the plugin include arbitrary local files and run any PHP they contain. Version 45.16.1 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-486c1c7c-5a66-42d3-85b0-13ce52a16ed1.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Automation Web Platform <= 4.8.6 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via 'wawp_custom_fields' Parameter
item.description:
The Automation Web Platform (Notifications and OTP for WooCommerce) plugin exposes a public REST route, `POST /wp-json/wawp/v1/signup/<op>`, with no permission enforcement. Its `finish_registration_logic` function writes the caller-supplied `wawp_custom_fields` parameter straight into `update_user_meta()` with no key allowlist. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore register an account whose `wp_capabilities` and `wp_user_level` meta make it an administrator. Version 4.8.7 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-f17d3e43-29c6-4c80-912d-53ceda3fcb5d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Online Scheduling and Appointment Booking System <= 28.2 - Insecure Direct Object Reference to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Booking Token Disclosure and Deletion via 'order_id' Parameter
item.description:
Bookly <= 28.2 has an unauthenticated IDOR in its booking-flow AJAX handlers. `bookly_get_form_id` stores an attacker-supplied `order_id` from `form_data` into a fresh booking session without checking that the session created that order. `bookly_render_complete` then trusts it and returns the Order's secret token. With that token, attackers can pull appointment data via `bookly_add_to_calendar` and permanently delete non-completed bookings via `bookly_rollback_order`. The issue is fixed in 28.3.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-d45a01e5-0e69-4d95-b609-b9002b3776da.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Customer Reviews for WooCommerce <= 5.120.0 - Missing Authorization to Unauthenticated Arbitrary Attachment Deletion via 'items[][media]' Parameter
item.description:
Customer Reviews for WooCommerce up to 5.120.0 lacks an authorization check in its review-submission handling, so an unauthenticated visitor can inject arbitrary Media Library attachment IDs through the `items[][media]` parameter of a review. When that review is later trashed and purged, the referenced attachments are permanently deleted. Version 5.121.0 fixes the flaw.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-b7bbeeea-3888-42a6-8d14-f5c39f5dcb70.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Request a Quote for WooCommerce <= 2.9.2 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via AJAX Popup Handler
item.description:
The Request a Quote for WooCommerce plugin (<= 2.9.2) does not validate file extension or MIME type in `afrfq_submit_quote_via_popup()`, the AJAX handler for the multi-page popup quote flow. It passes the attacker-supplied filename straight to `move_uploaded_file()` as the destination. An unauthenticated attacker can therefore drop an executable file such as a `.php` script into a web-accessible temporary RFQ upload directory, which typically leads to remote code execution. No patched version is available.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-3417ec27-6abf-45c7-945f-6ef456ba1187.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: miniOrange OTP Login, Verification and SMS Notifications <= 5.5.5 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via 'mo_wp_login_intent' Parameter
item.description:
The miniOrange OTP Login, Verification and SMS Notifications plugin allows an unauthenticated attacker to log in as any existing administrator using only a known username, an empty password, and a POST parameter `mo_wp_login_intent=otp`. The flaw is in `mo_by_pass_login()`: in the `skip_pass_fallback`-enabled branch it lacks a password-intent guard and treats administrator role membership as sufficient authentication. It is exploitable only when a specific combination of plugin options is enabled. Version 5.5.6 fixes it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-2895f0c2-41b6-4b11-9865-3bded4402aa9.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 <= 3.5.50 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via Signature Form Field
item.description:
Ultra Addons for Contact Form 7 versions up to and including 3.5.50 fail to properly validate file types in `uacf7_wpcf7_mail_components()`, allowing unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files through the signature form field. Because the uploaded file type is not restricted, this can lead to remote code execution. The flaw is only reachable when the plugin's PDF Generator module is enabled (it is disabled by default). Version 3.5.51 patches it.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-872e1a05-aacc-44fa-93c1-8c3f7b2fb46d.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: Appointment Booking Plugin <= 5.7.0 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary Shortcode Execution via First/Last Name Field
item.description:
LatePoint (Appointment Booking Plugin) versions up to and including 5.7.0 allow unauthenticated attackers to plant a shortcode payload in the first/last name field during the booking flow. When the Customer Cabinet block, rendered by `render_customer_dashboard()`, outputs the stored name into the content stream, WordPress core's `do_shortcode` filter (priority 11) re-parses it and executes it. The result is arbitrary shortcode execution. The issue is fixed in 5.7.1.
Digest entry: issues/security/wfi-c9a030c0-6129-40b0-81da-4c420929d198.md · Source: Wordfence Intelligence

item.title: #82816: Enable editableRoot for the list item block for multi-selection on mobile
item.description:
The list item block now opts into the private `editableRoot` editing-host mechanism (the same setting the paragraph block received in #81542), enabling native touch selection to extend across multiple list items on mobile. The PR also reverts the approach from #81042 that stripped `contenteditable` and `tabindex` from hosted fields, instead keeping the field editable and focusable so focus does not fall through to the `ul` or a parent container. An iOS-specific guard prevents the mousedown handler from cancelling double-tap word selection.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-82816.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg

item.title: #82566: Searchable selects: Hide creatable footer when it is filtered out
item.description:
`SearchableSelect` and `SearchableChipSelect` (and `SearchableChipSelectControl`) in `@wordpress/ui` now render the `creatable: true` footer item only when that item survives Base UI's filtering. Previously the footer always mounted from the original `items` prop, so after an unmatched query the Create row was still clickable but unreachable with Arrow Down. The components no longer clone or rewrite the filter and item groups to pin Create back into the keyboard list; keeping the creatable item in the filtered set is now the consumer's responsibility.
Digest entry: issues/gutenberg/gh-gutenberg-82566.md · Source: WordPress/gutenberg
